messages:
alex-customer: Hey folks — running into a production issue where streaming tool calls sometimes end up with partial/malformed JSON args and the tool errors out. Example error: \"invalid JSON: unexpected end of input\" and our schema validator says missing required field 'url'.

jess-support: Ugh, sorry about that. Can you paste a short curl repro and the request id from the failed call? Also which SDK / proxy are you using?

alex-customer: Using our server with the Node SDK v0.13 behind nginx reverse proxy. Request id from Redwood logs: rwd-req-2026-03-12-9a2f. Minimal repro we used: 

```bash
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"input":"call tool","stream":true,"tool":{"name":"fetch","args":{"url":"https://api.partner.local/health","method":"GET"}}}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```

Note: when streaming, the partner sees a truncated JSON body that ends like: `...\"args\":{\"url\":\"https://api.partner.local/health\",\"met` and then connection closes.

jess-support: Thanks. That looks like payload truncation mid-token. Two quick questions: 1) does the SDK emit any client-side error before the request finishes? 2) can you reproduce without nginx in front?

alex-customer: No client-side error, request completes from our side (200-ish) but the downstream tool returns schema validation error. We tried bypassing nginx (direct to Node) and it still happens ~30% of the time.

liam-eng: Looping in infra/obs. Does the Redwood ingress/proxy show any truncated receive logs for rwd-req-2026-03-12-9a2f? @maria-obs any recent deploys that touched the streaming path?

maria-obs: deploy-bot: inbound-proxy/1.4.2 deployed to prod at 2026-03-12T02:13Z :rocket: 

deploy-bot: deployment inbound-proxy/1.4.2 finished (sha: a1b2c3) — changes: improved keepalive handling, chunk buffering, misc bugfixes.

liam-eng: Hmm the keepalive/chunk buffering change may be related. We saw a rare case where chunk boundaries were dropped when upstream closed immediately after last chunk; that could leave the final bytes lost.

jess-support: For immediate mitigation: can you switch to non-streaming for tool calls (stream:false) or add a small timeout/retry on the partner side to request the missing field? I know non-ideal but buys time.

alex-customer: Can do switch to non-streaming for critical paths. For root cause we need logs. I captured server-side request dump for rwd-req-2026-03-12-9a2f: 

```text
RECEIVED_BODY_BYTES: 15342
EXPECTED_CONTENT_LENGTH: chunked
LAST_CHUNK_BYTES: 9
TRAILER: <none>
RAW_END: ...\"met
```

This matches the truncated snippet.

liam-eng: Thanks. We'll add a temporary debug patch to inbound-proxy to log full raw chunk boundaries for a short window. Can you DM me any additional request ids if you see more? Also we'll try to reproduce at higher volume.

maria-obs: Adding guard in router to flush final chunk before upstream close. Rolling a 1.4.3 canary to staging now.

jess-support: Alex, I filed ticket SUP-2026-289 with the tracing info and pinned the workaround. We'll monitor. If you can share additional request ids that show the truncated payload that helps. :pray:

alex-customer: Thanks all — will roll non-streaming for a few endpoints and send any more ids. Appreciate the quick triage.

liam-eng: Follow-ups: create an e2e test that sends streaming request with tiny final chunk, assert assembled body matches. If canary looks good we'll promote inbound-proxy/1.4.3 to prod.

jess-support: Closing this thread once the canary is green and your non-streaming workaround is validated. :white_check_mark:
